recipes.title: Quick Mozzarella for Neapolitan Pizza
recipes.description: A quick mozzarella recipe using citric acid, designed for high-heat pizza baking.

instructions.text: Dilute citric acid in 125ml water. Add to cold milk and stir well.
Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Dilute rennet in 1/4 cup cool water.
Add rennet to milk, stir gently for 30 seconds. Let set until clean break (about 5-10 min).
Cut curds into 1-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat curds to 105°F (40°C) while stirring gently.
Drain curds in colander for about 5 minutes.
Heat water to 185°F (85°C). Place drained curds in colander and submerge in hot water for 1 minute.
Remove curds and knead, folding corners inward to smooth. Repeat heating and kneading 5 times total.
Add salt during the final two kneading repetitions.
Shape into balls and immediately place in ice water to set shape.
For pizza use: salt the mozzarella and place between paper towels with a plate on top to reduce moisture before baking.

notes: Non-homogenized milk produces better texture
If mozzarella doesn't stretch well, check milk freshness and acidity
For better melting on pizza, try traditionally cultured mozzarella instead

recipes.title: Halloumi Cheese (Basic Method)
recipes.description: Traditional Cypriot cheese that can be grilled or fried without melting. Simple recipe requiring no starter culture.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add rennet and stir gently.
Wait approximately 30 minutes until milk sets firmly.
Break up curds and place into muslin cloth in two portions.
Drain whey back into pan. Let curds stand in muslin for about 30 minutes.
Heat the collected whey to boiling point (212°F/100°C).
Remove soft curds from muslin and place into the boiling whey.
Simmer gently for approximately 20 minutes until cheese floats to top.
Remove cheese, sprinkle with salt if desired, fold in half while still warm.
Apply weight on top and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Store in jar with small amount of whey, kept cool.

notes: Sheep milk yields about 1 kg cheese from 4 liters; cow milk needs 9 liters for same yield
No starter culture required - this is a forgiving cheese
If pH drops below 6 before boiling, texture will suffer
Target salt level: 1.5-2% based on taste preference
Halloumi won't melt when grilled due to its high pH

recipes.title: Traditional Feta Cheese
recipes.description: Classic Greek-style brined cheese. Longer aging produces more crumbly texture.

instructions.text: Warm milk to 85°F (29.5°C).
Add starter culture and mix thoroughly with a whisk until uniform.
Allow milk to ripen for 2 hours at 85°F.
Dissolve rennet in 3-4 tablespoons cool water (hot water destroys rennet).
Pour rennet slowly into milk while stirring constantly for at least 5 minutes.
Allow milk to set 1-2 hours until firm curds form with a clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2 inch cubes using a long knife.
Let curds rest 10 minutes, then cut any larger pieces.
Allow curds to sit 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drain whey by pouring through a cheesecloth-lined colander.
Tie cloth corners and hang to drain for 5 hours.
Transfer cheese to rectangular container (about 1 inch thick) and refrigerate 90 minutes.
Remove and cut into 1-inch cubes.
Prepare brine: dissolve 1.5 cups salt in 1 quart warm water, then cool.
Place cheese cubes in COLD brine solution and refrigerate for 5-30 days.
Pat dry with paper towel before serving. Store in airtight container.

notes: Longer brining (up to 30 days) produces more crumbly, tangy feta
If using cow milk, add lipase for more authentic piquant flavor
Raw milk requires minimum 60 days aging for safety
Ultra-pasteurized milk will not work for this recipe

recipes.title: Gouda Cheese
recipes.description: Classic Dutch washed-curd cheese with sweet, mild flavor. Can be aged from 4 weeks to over a year.

instructions.text: Warm milk to 85°F (29.5°C). Add starter culture and mix thoroughly.
Dissolve rennet in 3-4 tablespoons cool water, then stir into milk for 5+ minutes.
Allow milk to set 1-2 hours until firm curds form.
Cut curds into 1/2 inch cubes and let sit 10 minutes.
Gradually raise temperature to 102°F (39°C) over 45 minutes, stirring gently every few minutes.
Remove 3 cups whey and replace with equal amount of 102°F water. This is the 'washing' step.
Repeat whey replacement every 15 minutes for 45 minutes (three total replacements).
Drain whey through cheesecloth-lined mold.
Press at 20 lbs (9 kg) for 45 minutes.
Flip cheese and press at 40 lbs (18 kg) for 3 hours.
Prepare cold brine and float cheese for 3 hours, flipping every 45 minutes.
Pat dry and refrigerate for minimum 25 days, flipping daily.
Monitor for mold - treat with vinegar-dampened paper towels as needed.
Optional: wax cheese for extended aging (3+ months).

notes: The 'washing' step (replacing whey with water) removes lactose, creating Gouda's characteristic sweetness
Young Gouda: 4-8 weeks aging. Mature Gouda: 8-17+ weeks
Wax after 3 weeks of aging if planning long-term storage
Flora Danica culture adds buttery diacetyl notes
Higher pressing weights (up to 50 lbs) create denser texture

recipes.title: Traditional Cultured Mozzarella
recipes.description: Authentic mozzarella made with thermophilic cultures for superior flavor and melt. Takes longer but produces better results than quick methods.

ingredients.item: thermophilic culture C201 (ST, LB, LH strains)

instructions.text: Heat milk to target temperature: 32°C (90°F) for softer mozzarella, or 37°C (99°F) for firmer pizza-style.
Add thermophilic culture and yogurt. Mix well.
Add lipase if desired for more traditional flavor.
Let culture ripen for 1 hour before adding rennet.
Add diluted rennet and stir gently for 1 minute.
Allow to set until clean break (40-60 minutes).
Cut curds into 1/2 inch cubes.
Let curds rest, then slowly heat to 40°C (104°F) over 30 minutes.
Monitor pH - target 5.2-5.4 before stretching.
Drain curds and let acidify until stretchy when tested in hot water.
Heat water to 170-180°F (77-82°C). Stretch curds in hot water, kneading until smooth and glossy.
Shape into balls and cool in ice water or light brine.

notes: 32°C produces softer mozzarella for fresh eating (caprese, etc.)
37°C produces firmer mozzarella better suited for pizza
The 1-hour culture ripening before rennet is key for flavor development
Test stretch readiness: a small piece in hot water should stretch without breaking
Cultured mozzarella melts better than quick citric acid versions

recipes.title: Queso Panela (Mexican Fresh Cheese)
recipes.description: A mild, white Mexican cheese that softens when heated but doesn't melt. Perfect for grilling or frying.

instructions.text: Pour milk into pot. Dissolve powdered milk over medium heat without boiling.
Dilute calcium chloride in 1/4 cup boiled water and add to warm milk, stirring well.
Remove from heat. Dissolve rennet in 1/4 cup water and add to milk, stirring gently.
Let stand for 20 minutes to form curd.
Cut curd into 1-inch cubes. Let rest 20+ minutes.
Heat gently while stirring.
Strain whey through cheesecloth-lined colander.
Add salt to curds and knead lightly.
Place in colander with cheesecloth, apply weight, and press for several hours, turning halfway.
Once cheese releases no more whey, store in airtight container in refrigerator.

notes: Shelf life approximately 15 days refrigerated
Softens when heated but doesn't melt - ideal for grilling
Milk powder increases protein content for better curd formation

recipes.title: Spiced Paneer (Indian Fresh Cheese)
recipes.description: Traditional Indian cheese with jalapeño and cumin, perfect for curries or pan-frying.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 180-190°F (82-88°C).
Hold milk at temperature for 20-30 minutes.
Add citric acid or lemon juice slowly while stirring. Curds should form immediately.
Once curds separate clearly from whey, remove from heat.
Drain through cheesecloth-lined colander.
Mix salt, jalapeño, and cumin into drained curds.
Place curds between two dinner plates.
Add heavy weight and refrigerate for 4-6 hours.
Cut into cubes for cooking.

notes: Longer pressing creates firmer cheese
Can substitute lime juice for lemon juice
Paneer doesn't melt - perfect for sautéing in curries

recipes.title: Appenzeller Swiss Cheese
recipes.description: Traditional Swiss-style cheese with a washed rind, aged minimum 1 year. Includes detailed pH targets for consistent results.

instructions.text: Heat milk to ~90°F. Target starting pH: 6.75
Add cultures and ripen. Add rennet when pH drops ≥0.1
Allow flocculation (25-35 minutes).
Cut curds to 1/8 inch. Maintain pH 6.35 at whey pitch.
Cook curd to ~120°F over 60 minutes (max 1°F per minute).
Pitch curds for 5 minutes.
Press in warm whey: 1 hour with low weight, flipping 2-4 times.
Press outside whey: 40 min at 25 lbs, 1 hr at 25 lbs, 2 hr at 50 lbs, 4 hr at 50 lbs.
Brine: 6 hours per pound at 18% salt. Target pH in brine: 5.4
Air dry 12 hours, then age at 50-55°F, 80-85% humidity.
Wash daily for 2 weeks, then weekly for 2 months.
Age minimum 1 year for full flavor development.

notes: pH targets: Start 6.75 → Whey pitch 6.35 → Brine 5.4
Add 5g CaCl2 + 5ml white vinegar per gallon to brine
Washed rind develops during aging
Minimum 1 year aging for authentic flavor

recipes.title: Cheddasiago (Cheddared Thermophilic Cheese)
recipes.description: Experimental cheese combining Asiago's thermophilic cultures with cheddar's cheddaring process.
recipes.servings_yield: About 1 lb 13 oz from 9 liters milk

instructions.text: Combine milk and cream for ~3.8% butterfat.
Heat to 95°F. Add cultures and ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Wait for clean break.
Cut curds to 3/8 inch cubes.
Gradually raise temperature to 115°F over 45 minutes with gentle stirring.
Continue stirring until curds reach pea size and pass grip test.
Drain whey. Consolidate curds into 1-inch thick layer.
Cheddar: Place warm water on curds for 15 minutes. Repeat 4 times over 1.5 hours, targeting pH 5.3.
Mill curds, add salt, mix well.
Press: 30 lbs increasing to 170 lbs overnight.
Air dry 2-3 days at 55°F.
Wax in red coating. Age minimum 3 months (6+ recommended).

notes: Target pH 5.3 after cheddaring
Red wax is traditional for visual appeal
Longer aging (6+ months) develops more complex flavor

recipes.title: Tvorog (Russian Farmer's Cheese)
recipes.source_note: CheeseForum.org - Fresh Cheeses (reconstructed from forum discussion)
recipes.description: A soft, fresh Russian-style cheese similar to quark. Mild, tangy, and versatile for sweet or savory dishes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to lukewarm (about 85-90°F/30-32°C) - it should feel neutral to the touch.
Stir in the buttermilk and mix well.
Cover and let sit at room temperature for 24-48 hours until the milk has thickened and set like yogurt.
Line a colander with cheesecloth or butter muslin and set over a bowl.
Gently pour or ladle the thickened milk into the lined colander.
Let drain for 2-4 hours for a creamy texture, or overnight for a drier, crumbly texture.
Season with salt if desired.
Transfer to a container and refrigerate. Use within 1 week.

notes: No rennet required - this is a purely lactic-set cheese
Use as you would ricotta or quark
Traditional in Russian blintzes (syrniki) and pierogi fillings
Can be sweetened with sugar for desserts

flags: Recipe reconstructed from forum discussion of traditional method

recipes.title: 18% Brine for Cheese Making
recipes.description: A saturated salt brine solution used for brining cheeses like feta, gouda, and other aged varieties.

ingredients.item: non-iodized salt (sea salt or cheese salt)

instructions.text: Heat 1/2 gallon of water to dissolve the salt more easily.
Add salt gradually, stirring until fully dissolved. The solution should be saturated.
Add remaining water to cool the solution.
Add calcium chloride to prevent calcium leaching from cheese.
Add vinegar to lower pH and prevent bacterial growth.
Cool brine to 50-55°F before using.
Store in refrigerator. Brine can be reused multiple times.

notes: Check salinity with a brine hydrometer or egg float test
Brine time varies by cheese
Never use iodized salt

recipes.title: Tilsit (Washed Rind Cheese)
recipes.description: A semi-hard washed-rind cheese with a pungent aroma and tangy flavor from East Prussia.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add cultures and B. linens, ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk. Add diluted rennet.
Let set 45-60 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat curds to 100°F (38°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Maintain temperature and stir for 30 more minutes.
Drain whey and transfer curds to cheese mold.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 minutes, flip, then 20 lbs for 6-8 hours.
Brine in saturated salt solution for 8-12 hours.
Age at 50-55°F, 90% humidity. Wash rind every 2-3 days for first 2 weeks.
Continue aging 2-4 months, washing weekly.

notes: B. linens creates the characteristic orange rind
Similar to Limburger but milder

recipes.title: English Coulommiers
recipes.description: A soft-ripened bloomy rind cheese similar to Brie but smaller and creamier.

instructions.text: Heat milk (and cream if using) to 90°F (32°C).
Sprinkle cultures and molds over surface. Stir in after 2 minutes.
Ripen for 90 minutes at 90°F.
Add calcium chloride if using, then diluted rennet.
Let set 90 minutes until very firm clean break.
Cut curds into 1-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Gently ladle curds into Coulommiers molds.
Let drain at room temperature, flipping every few hours, for 24 hours.
Unmold and salt all surfaces lightly.
Age at 50-55°F, 90-95% humidity. Flip daily for first week.
White mold should cover cheese in 10-14 days.
Wrap in cheese paper when fully ripened. Best at 4-6 weeks.

notes: Coulommiers is essentially a larger, thicker Camembert
Best eaten at room temperature

recipes.title: Traditional Cheddar
recipes.description: Classic English cheddar using the traditional cheddaring technique.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add culture and ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45-60 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/4-inch cubes. Let heal 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 102°F (39°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at 102°F for 30-45 minutes, stirring.
Drain whey to level of curds. Let curds mat for 15 minutes.
Cut curd mass into slabs. Stack and flip every 15 minutes for 2 hours (cheddaring).
Mill cheddared slabs into finger-sized pieces.
Add salt, mix thoroughly.
Pack into cloth-lined mold. Press at 10 lbs for 15 minutes.
Flip, press at 30 lbs for 12 hours. Flip, press 30 lbs for 12 more hours.
Air dry 2-3 days until rind forms.
Wax or bandage wrap. Age at 55°F for 3-12 months.

notes: Cheddaring develops the characteristic texture
Sharp cheddar requires 9-12 months aging

recipes.title: Jarlsberg-Style Cheese
recipes.description: Norwegian-style Swiss cheese with characteristic large eyes and mild, nutty flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add thermophilic culture and Propionic shermanii.
Ripen for 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk, then diluted rennet.
Let set 30-45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/4-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 102°F (39°C) over 30 minutes.
Continue heating slowly to 108°F (42°C) over 15 minutes.
Hold at 108°F, stirring, for 30-45 minutes.
Let curds settle 5 minutes. Drain whey.
Transfer curds to mold. Press at 10 lbs for 30 minutes.
Flip, press at 20 lbs for 2 hours. Flip, press at 30 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine in saturated salt solution for 12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days.
Age at 55°F for 2 weeks, then 65-70°F for 2-3 weeks for eye development.
Return to 55°F and age 2-3 months total.

notes: The warm room period is crucial for eye development
Propionic bacteria create CO2 which forms the holes

recipes.title: Monterey Jack
recipes.description: A mild, creamy American cheese perfect for melting.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 88°F (31°C). Add culture and ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 100°F (38°C) over 30 minutes.
Hold at 100°F, stirring, for 30 minutes.
Let curds settle 5 minutes. Drain whey.
Stir curds to release more whey. Add salt and mix.
Transfer to mold. Press at 10 lbs for 15 minutes.
Flip, press at 20 lbs for 30 minutes. Flip, press at 40 lbs for 12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days, flipping twice daily.
Wax or vacuum seal. Age at 55°F for 1-3 months.

notes: For Pepper Jack, add 2 tbsp diced jalapeños with the salt
Great melting cheese

recipes.title: Mysost (Norwegian Whey Cheese)
recipes.description: A sweet, caramel-flavored Scandinavian cheese made by reducing whey. Also known as Brunost.

instructions.text: Start with fresh, sweet whey from the same day's cheesemaking.
Pour whey into a large, heavy-bottomed pot. Add cream and milk if using.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to medium. Continue boiling and stirring as liquid reduces.
As volume decreases (2-3 hours), stir more frequently. Mixture will turn tan, then brown.
When reduced to about 1/4 volume and thick like caramel sauce, remove from heat.
Beat vigorously with wooden spoon for 5-10 minutes as it cools.
Pour into a buttered mold while still pourable.
Refrigerate until firm.

notes: Goat whey produces traditional Gjetost
Constant stirring prevents burning
Traditional Norwegian breakfast

recipes.title: Ricotta Salata
recipes.description: A firm, salted, aged ricotta that can be sliced or grated. Traditional Sicilian cheese.

instructions.text: Combine whey and milk in a large pot. Heat to 200°F (93°C).
Add citric acid solution. Stir gently. Curds will form.
Remove from heat. Let sit 10 minutes.
Skim curds into cheesecloth-lined colander.
Let drain 30 minutes, then mix in salt.
Pack salted curds into a ricotta mold.
Press with 5 lbs weight for 12 hours. Flip and press another 12 hours.
Remove from mold. Rub exterior with additional salt.
Place on rack in refrigerator. Turn daily and salt lightly for 1 week.
Continue aging 2-4 weeks total.

notes: Salata means salted
Excellent crumbled over salads or pasta

recipes.title: Bel Paese
recipes.description: A mild, creamy Italian semi-soft cheese with buttery flavor. Great for beginners.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture and ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Gently stir curds for 20 minutes at 90°F.
Let curds settle. Drain whey to curd level.
Transfer curds to mold. Press lightly at 5 lbs for 30 minutes.
Flip and press at 10 lbs for 6-8 hours.
Brine for 6-8 hours.
Air dry 1-2 days.
Age at 50°F, 85% humidity for 6-8 weeks. Wax after 2 weeks.

notes: Bel Paese means 'beautiful country'
Good melting cheese

recipes.title: Gouda
recipes.description: A classic Dutch washed-curd cheese with smooth, creamy texture and sweet, nutty flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture and ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45-60 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Remove 1/3 of whey. Replace with same amount of 175°F water (washing step).
Stir gently while heating to 100°F (38°C) over 30 minutes.
Hold at 100°F, stirring, for 30 minutes.
Let curds settle and mat for 5 minutes. Drain whey.
Transfer curds to Gouda mold. Press at 10 lbs for 30 minutes.
Flip, press at 20 lbs for 2 hours. Flip, press at 30 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine for 12-24 hours (3 hours per pound).
Air dry 2-3 days, turning twice daily.
Wax with cheese wax. Age at 55°F for 2-12 months.

notes: Whey washing creates Gouda's characteristic sweetness
Aged Gouda develops caramel notes

recipes.title: Havarti
recipes.description: A Danish semi-soft cheese with small irregular holes and buttery, tangy flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add culture and ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Gently stir curds for 10 minutes at 86°F.
Remove 1/3 of whey. Add back same amount of 145°F water while stirring.
Continue stirring for 15 minutes. Temperature will rise to about 92°F.
Let curds settle 5 minutes. Drain whey.
Transfer curds to mold. Press at 10 lbs for 30 minutes.
Flip, press at 20 lbs for 6-8 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours.
Air dry 1-2 days.
Age at 50°F, 85% humidity for 2-3 months.

notes: Flora Danica culture creates the characteristic small holes
For Dill Havarti, add 2 tbsp dried dill with salt

recipes.title: Edam
recipes.description: A Dutch semi-hard cheese traditionally made with part-skim milk. Mild, slightly salty.

ingredients.item: part-skim milk or whole milk with 1 qt cream removed

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture and ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45-60 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Remove 1/3 of whey. Replace with 175°F water while stirring.
Heat to 100°F (38°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at 100°F, stirring, for 30 minutes.
Let curds settle. Drain whey.
Transfer curds to Edam mold. Press at 10 lbs for 30 minutes.
Flip, press at 20 lbs for 2 hours. Flip, press at 30 lbs for 10-12 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days.
Wax with red cheese wax. Age at 55°F for 2-4 months.

notes: Traditional Edam uses part-skim milk
Red wax is traditional for export

recipes.title: Mascarpone
recipes.description: A rich, creamy Italian cheese essential for tiramisu.

instructions.text: Pour cream into a double boiler or heavy saucepan.
Heat cream to 185°F (85°C), stirring occasionally.
Add tartaric acid solution (or lemon juice) and stir gently for 5 minutes.
Cream will thicken slightly. Remove from heat.
Let cool to room temperature, about 1 hour.
Line a colander with fine cheesecloth.
Pour thickened cream into cloth. Cover and refrigerate.
Drain 8-12 hours until thick and spreadable.
Transfer to container. Store refrigerated up to 1 week.

notes: Tartaric acid produces most authentic flavor
Do not use ultra-pasteurized cream
Essential for tiramisu

recipes.title: Petit Bleu (Small Blue Cheese)
recipes.description: A small-format blue cheese perfect for home cheesemakers.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add mesophilic culture and P. roqueforti.
Ripen 60 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 90 minutes until firm clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Gently stir curds every 5 minutes for 30 minutes at 86°F.
Let curds settle. Drain whey.
Gently ladle curds into blue cheese mold. Do not press.
Flip cheese every 15 minutes for first hour, then every few hours for 24 hours.
Remove from mold. Salt all surfaces thoroughly.
Age at 50°F, 95% humidity. Flip daily.
After 1 week, pierce cheese with needle every inch from top to bottom.
Continue aging 2-3 months.

notes: Piercing introduces oxygen for blue mold growth
High humidity prevents cracking

recipes.title: Paneer
recipes.description: A fresh Indian cheese that doesn't melt, perfect for curries and grilling.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 190°F (88°C), stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat. Add lemon juice or vinegar, stirring gently.
Curds will separate within 1-2 minutes. If not, add more acid.
Let sit 10 minutes off heat.
Line a colander with cheesecloth.
Pour curds and whey through cloth. Rinse briefly with cool water.
Add salt if using and mix gently.
Gather cloth and twist to squeeze out whey.
Form into a disk, press with heavy weight for 1-3 hours.
Cut into cubes. Use immediately or refrigerate in water.

notes: Does not melt - perfect for grilling or frying
Store submerged in water
Essential for palak paneer

recipes.title: Lucy's Feta (Chabichou-Style)
recipes.description: A tangy, crumbly feta-style cheese using lactic fermentation.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 72°F (22°C) - just below room temperature.
Add culture and stir. Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add very diluted rennet (just 2 drops). Stir gently.
Cover and let ferment at 68-72°F for 18-24 hours.
Curd will be solid. Ladle into cheesecloth-lined mold.
Let drain at room temperature 24 hours, flipping every 6-8 hours.
Remove from mold. Cut into 1-inch cubes.
Sprinkle liberally with salt, tossing to coat.
Let sit 2 days at room temperature, turning and resalting daily.
Transfer to jar and cover with 8% brine or olive oil. Refrigerate.
Ready after 1 week in brine.

notes: Very little rennet creates lactic texture
Sheep milk makes authentic Greek-style feta

recipes.title: Whole Milk Ricotta
recipes.description: Creamy, fresh ricotta made from whole milk.

instructions.text: Combine milk, cream, and salt in a large pot.
Heat to 190°F (88°C), stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat. Add lemon juice and stir gently.
Let sit undisturbed 5-10 minutes. Curds will form.
Line a colander with cheesecloth.
Gently ladle curds into cloth.
Let drain 1-2 hours for creamy ricotta.
Transfer to container. Refrigerate up to 5 days.

notes: The cream makes this richer than traditional ricotta
Save the whey for bread baking

recipes.title: Farmhouse Cheddar
recipes.description: A simplified cheddar without the traditional cheddaring step. Easier for beginners.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture and ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/4-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 100°F (38°C) over 30 minutes.
Hold at 100°F, stirring, for 30 minutes.
Let curds settle 5 minutes. Drain whey.
Stir curds to release more whey. Add salt and mix.
Transfer to mold. Press at 10 lbs for 15 minutes.
Flip, press at 20 lbs for 30 minutes. Flip, press at 40 lbs for 12 hours.
Air dry 2-4 days until rind forms.
Wax or vacuum seal. Age at 55°F for 2-6 months.

notes: Skipping cheddaring produces a moister, milder cheese
Great introduction to hard cheese making

recipes.title: Queso Fresco
recipes.description: A fresh Mexican cheese, ready to eat the same day. Mild and crumbly.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 32°C (90°F).
Add culture and mix thoroughly.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add diluted rennet, stir 1 minute only, then cover.
Allow 45-60 minutes for clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2cm (1/4 inch) cubes.
Slowly raise temperature to 35°C (95°F) over 20 minutes with gentle stirring.
Cover and rest curds 5 minutes.
Drain whey by hand, return curds to pot.
Add salt, mix gently, rest 30 minutes at 35°C.
Line mould with cheesecloth, fill with curds.
Press at 16kg (35lbs) for six hours.
Remove from press. Store refrigerated up to 2 weeks.

notes: Can be consumed immediately or aged slightly
Great for tacos and enchiladas

recipes.title: Chili Queso Fresco
recipes.description: A spiced variation of queso fresco with dried chili flakes for heat.

instructions.text: Crush dried chilies and combine with 3 tbsp water. Boil for 15 minutes.
Strain, reserving the chili-infused water and chili flakes separately.
Add chili water to milk when heating to target temperature.
Follow standard queso fresco procedure through curd cutting.
Incorporate chili flakes during the milling and resting phases.
Add salt and mix well.
Press for 6 hours (no unwrapping needed during pressing).
Cheese is ready immediately but improves after 24 hours refrigeration.

notes: Salt can be increased slightly for saltier preference
Ideal for beginner cheesemakers

recipes.title: Kaffeost (Swedish Coffee Cheese)
recipes.description: Traditional Swedish cheese served in hot coffee. Originally made from reindeer milk.
recipes.total_time: Several hours including draining and baking

instructions.text: Pour milk and cream into saucepan. Warm to 37°C (body temperature).
Remove from heat, mix in rennet, let stand 30-40 minutes until solidified.
Gently stir with slotted spoon while reheating to lukewarm.
Heat mixture toward boiling point (do not boil). Remove just before whey boils.
Place cheese in colander and press out whey with weights for several hours.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Press dried cheese into greased casserole (max 3 cm thick).
Bake until browned.
Wrap warm cheese edges in foil if hardened. Cool completely.
Cut into cubes or strips. Place in coffee cup and pour hot coffee over.

notes: Leftover cheese can be frozen
Also served with cloudberries or raspberry coulis
Whey can be used for bread

recipes.title: Tzafatit (Cheese from Tzfat)
recipes.description: A soft, salty Israeli cheese with ancient roots. Traditionally paired with watermelon.

instructions.text: Warm milk to 37°C (99°F).
Add culture, calcium chloride, vinegar, and rennet while stirring.
Hold the heat for 40 minutes without moving pot.
Cut curds into 0.5 cm cubes. Rest for 10 minutes.
Stir the curds slowly for 15 minutes.
Remove whey until reaching curd level.
Add the salt and mix through for around 2 minutes.
Place in small hoops, flipping every 15 minutes for one hour.
Let sit for 12 hours draining.
Refrigerate. Ready to consume the next day.

notes: Traditional pairing with watermelon
Soft and salty texture

recipes.title: Romano Pepato
recipes.description: Peppered Romano cheese with added peppercorns for sharpness and flavor.

instructions.text: Add 1 tbsp peppercorns to 1/2 cup water. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Strain peppercorns, reserving the pepper water.
Add pepper water to ripened milk before rennet addition.
Continue standard Romano procedure through curd draining.
Mill 1 tbsp peppercorns through curds. Distribute evenly.
Press according to Romano recipe.
Brine for 24 hours (for 1 kg cheese).
Age according to Romano recipe (6+ months).

notes: For milder flavor, omit pepper water and add only peppercorns at milling
Follow base Romano recipe for detailed steps

flags: Builds on base Romano recipe not fully detailed

recipes.title: Halloumi (Cypriot Cheese)
recipes.description: A Cypriot cheese that can be grilled without melting. Traditionally made with mint.

instructions.text: Sanitize all equipment.
Heat milk to 32°C (90°F) and add rennet solution. Turn off heat.
Stir, cover, and allow setting for 40 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 12mm cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Gently heat milk to 40°C (104°F) over 20 minutes.
Rest curds 10 minutes. Drain whey through cheesecloth for 3 minutes.
Press curds under 4kg weight for 10 minutes. Flip and press for 20 minutes.
Heat reserved whey to 97°C. Skim excess curd froth.
Cut pressed curd into rectangles. Place in hot whey.
After ~45 minutes when cheese floats, leave 15 more minutes.
Remove pieces. Coat with salt and mint. Fold while hot.
Drain 1 hour. Refrigerate or vacuum-pack.

notes: Allow 24 hours before using for salt to permeate
Store in airtight containers up to 1 week or vacuum-pack for 6 months

recipes.title: Italian Bag Cheese
recipes.description: A tight-textured Italian cheese similar to mozzarella, made by heating curds in whey.

instructions.text: Add milk to pot. Add calcium chloride if using homogenized milk.
Heat milk to 30°C (86°F). Add culture, stir 30 seconds.
Add rennet solution, stir 1 minute. Cover, wait 45 minutes for clean break.
Cut curds into 13mm (1/2 inch) cubes without stirring.
Line colander with cheesecloth. Ladle curds in, saving whey.
Gather cloth forming a bag. Hang over whey pot, drain 30 minutes.
Untie, turn cheese over. Re-tie and hang for 1 hour.
Tie bag tightly. Place in original pot with saved whey.
Heat to 88°C (190°F) over 20 minutes.
Turn off heat. Leave cheese in whey until cool (about 5 hours).
Remove bag, hang for 2 hours until dripping stops.
Place firm cheese in saturated brine for 2 hours.
Remove, eat fresh or air dry 4 hours. Refrigerate up to 2 weeks.

notes: Yields tight texture like mozzarella when refrigerated
Great with fresh tomatoes, cucumbers, and basil

recipes.title: Homemade Cream Cheese
recipes.description: A creamy, tangy cream cheese far superior to processed varieties.

instructions.text: Sanitize all equipment via boiling or weak bleach solution.
Add calcium chloride solution to milk if needed. Stir 30 seconds.
Warm milk to 30°C (86°F).
Add culture, stir for one minute.
Add 3 tsp rennet solution, stir for two minutes.
Cover and rest at room temperature (~21°C/70°F) for 18 hours.
Line colander with 4-layer cheesecloth. Ladle curds in.
Form a bag and drain for 12 hours using a double granny knot.
Remove cheese and work in salt gradually.
Refrigerate in airtight container for about two weeks.

notes: Takes time but produces superior results
Creamy texture with slight tanginess

recipes.title: Camembert
recipes.description: A soft-ripened French cheese with white mold rind and creamy interior.

instructions.text: Sterilize all equipment in boiling water for 15 minutes.
Heat milk to 32°C (90°F). Add starter culture and P. candidum. Cover and ripen 90 minutes.
Maintain temperature, add rennet, stir 2 minutes. Cover until clean break (60 minutes).
Cut into 1.25cm cubes. Stir gently at target temperature for 15 minutes.
Allow curds to settle 15 minutes. Drain whey to curd level.
Place four hoops on sushi mats. Gently ladle curds until full.
Drain at room temperature for 1 hour.
Flip cheeses hourly for 5 hours using mats to support.
Remove hoops carefully. Sprinkle with salt, rub gently all over.
Store in ripening box at 7°C (45°F) with 85% humidity for 5 days.
Flip after 5 days. Continue aging until white mould covers surface (7-10 days).
Wrap in cheese paper. Continue aging 3 weeks total.

notes: Fill hoops only once - overfilling causes collapse
Pick off any black mould with sterile knife
Consider adding Geotrichum candidum to reduce slipperiness

recipes.title: Drunken Cow Cheese (Formaggio Ubriaco)
recipes.description: A cow's milk cheese bathed in red wine, developing deep flavor and purple rind.

ingredients.item: sweet red wine (dark Lambrusco or Crimson Cabernet)

instructions.text: Pour milk into pot. Add diluted calcium chloride and stir.
Heat milk to 32°C (90°F). Mix in diluted starter culture. Ripen 10 minutes.
Add diluted rennet, stir 1 minute. Cover, set for 1 hour until clean break.
Cut curds into 1cm (1/2") cubes. Stir gently 1 minute, rest 5 minutes.
Draw off 1/3 of whey. Gradually add 80°C water, stirring to raise temp to 33°C (92°F).
Rest 10 minutes at 33°C, stirring occasionally.
Drain whey to curd level. Continue adding 80°C water to reach 38°C (100°F).
Maintain 38°C for 15 minutes with stirring. Rest 30 minutes.
Strain whey. Return curds, mill into 6mm pieces. Blend in salt.
Pack into 900gm mold. Press at 10kg for 20 minutes.
Turn, rewrap, press at 10kg for 20 hours. Turn again, press 12 hours.
Remove from press. Skewer holes halfway through each end.
Submerge in red wine for 24 hours. Flip at 12 hours.
Remove, dry on mats 6 hours. Repeat wine bath for another 24 hours.
Dry until touch-dry. Age at 11°C (52°F), 80-85% humidity for 3 months.
Turn daily for first 2 weeks. Wipe with brine if mould develops.

notes: Washed curd technique reduces acidity
Creamy texture with wine-infused flavor

recipes.title: Komijnekaas (Dutch Cumin Cheese)
recipes.description: A Dutch spiced cheese with cumin and caraway seeds based on farmhouse cheddar.

instructions.text: Boil cumin and caraway seeds in 3/4 cup water for 15 minutes. Strain, reserve liquid and seeds separately.
Heat milk to 33°C. Add calcium chloride solution.
Add seed-infused water to milk at target temperature.
Add culture and ripen. Add rennet and proceed with farmhouse cheddar method.
After milling curds, add 2 tbsp salt and the reserved seeds. Mix thoroughly.
Press into two 1 kg molds following farmhouse cheddar pressing schedule.
Air-dry cheese out of mold for one week before storage.
Age approximately two months.

notes: Based on farmhouse cheddar technique
The seed-infused water adds golden color

recipes.title: Wensleydale Cheese
recipes.description: A Yorkshire cheese with firm, slightly flaky texture and subtle sweetness.

instructions.text: Sterilize all equipment in boiling water for 15 minutes.
Using double boiler, warm milk to 30°C (86°F). Add calcium chloride if needed.
Mix in mesophilic starter. Cover and ripen for 45 minutes.
Add rennet while stirring for 2 minutes. Let set undisturbed for 45 minutes.
Cut into 13mm cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Stir for 10 minutes, rest 15 minutes, then stir while raising temperature to 32°C (90°F).
Maintain temperature, stirring often to prevent knitting, for 2 hours.
Drain whey and ladle curds into cheesecloth-lined colander.
Tie bundle, open every 15 minutes for 2 hours to break curds smaller.
Break up curd and apply salt. Mix thoroughly.
Layer half curds in basket, add sage leaves, add remaining curds.
Press at 5kg (10 lbs) for 15 minutes.
Remove, turn over, press at 25kg (50 lbs) for 12 hours.
Place on board and dry for 2 days. Apply wax.
Store at 13-15°C (55-59°F) at 80-85% humidity.

notes: Ready in 3 weeks but can age up to 3 months
Pairs well with fresh fruits

recipes.title: 30 Minute Mozzarella
recipes.description: Quick mozzarella made with citric acid and microwave stretching.

instructions.text: Sanitize all equipment and air dry completely.
Heat milk to 13°C, then add citric acid solution with calcium chloride. Add lipase and stir well.
Heat to 33°C (90°F). Add rennet solution, stir gently 1 minute.
Continue heating to 38-40°C. Curds should resemble scrambled eggs within 5-8 minutes.
Pour off whey. Transfer curds to cheesecloth-lined colander.
Drain whey from curds in Pyrex bowl. Microwave on high for 1 minute.
Drain whey again. Microwave 30 seconds, drain, form into single mass, microwave final 30 seconds.
Add salt and knead quickly like bread dough until smooth, shiny, and stretchy.
Form into balls and place in ice water 5-10 minutes to cool.

notes: Wear rubber gloves as curds become hot
Best used fresh, store in chilled whey

recipes.title: Caerphilly Cheese
recipes.description: A Welsh/English lightly pressed cheese that ripens in just 3 weeks. Mild with a slightly sour tang.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 32°C using double boiler. Add calcium chloride if using homogenized milk.
Add starter culture, stir 1 minute. Rest covered for 30 minutes.
Add diluted rennet, stir 2 minutes. Rest 40 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into uniform 6mm cubes.
Slowly raise temperature to 33°C over 10 minutes.
Hold at 33°C for 40 minutes with frequent stirring. Rest 5 minutes.
Drain curds through cheesecloth-lined colander for 5 minutes.
Cut drained curds into 2.5cm slabs. Stack and turn twice within 10 minutes.
Break curds into thumbnail-sized pieces. Blend with salt.
Fill cheesecloth-lined 1kg mould with salted curds.
Press at 5kg (10 lbs) for 10 minutes. Remove, salt both surfaces, rewrap.
Press at 5kg for 10 minutes, then 7.5kg (15 lbs) for 20 minutes.
Final press at 7.5kg for 16 hours.
Air dry on cheese mat for 3-4 days, turning several times daily.
Age at 13°C with 80-85% humidity for three weeks.

notes: No waxing needed - natural rind forms
High salt inhibits mould growth
Easy, quick cheese for beginners

recipes.title: Parmesan Cheese
recipes.description: Home-made version of the Italian classic, aged 10 months for hard, gritty texture.

ingredients.item: lite or semi-skimmed milk (1.4% or less fat)

instructions.text: Sterilize all equipment. Set up double boiler.
Heat milk to 35°C, alternating litre measurements for even mixing.
Add thermophilic culture. Rest 15 minutes covered.
Add calcium chloride, mix. Stir in lipase mixture for 1 minute.
Add rennet mix, stir minimum 1 minute. Cover, allow 45-minute coagulation.
Cut curds using balloon whisk to achieve ~4mm pieces.
Rest 5 minutes. Stir at 35°C for 10 minutes.
Increase temperature to 42°C over 30 minutes. Maintain 15 minutes with whisking.
Increase to 52°C over 30 minutes with regular stirring.
Curds should appear small-grained, dry, and squeaky. Rest 5 minutes.
Drain curds through cheesecloth-lined colander.
Form curd ball in mold. Press at 2.5kg for 15 minutes.
Unwrap, flip, rewrap. Press at 5kg for 30 minutes.
Press at 7.5kg for 2 hours. Final press at 10kg for 12 hours.
Immerse in room-temperature brine for 24 hours at 21°C, flipping occasionally.
Pat dry. Place on sushi mat in aging cave (13°C/80% humidity) for 10 months.
Turn daily first week, then weekly. Remove mold with brine-dampened cloth.
Wax at approximately three-week mark.

notes: Lipase inhibits rennet - increase rennet by 25% if using lipase
10-month aging creates characteristic hard, gritty texture

recipes.title: Homemade Feta
recipes.description: A brined Greek-style cheese with texture between Danish softness and Greek crumbliness.

instructions.text: Add calcium chloride solution to milk and stir 25 seconds.
Heat milk to 32°C and maintain throughout.
Mix in mesophilic starter and lipase solution. Do not exceed 40°C.
Allow milk to ripen undisturbed for 45 minutes.
Reheat to 32°C, add diluted rennet with quick stir. Do not reheat after this.
Wait ~40 minutes until curds form. Test firmness with finger.
Using whisk, gently stab vertically to create ~1cm cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Stir 2 minutes every 10 minutes for 2 hours at 32°C.
Pour through cheesecloth, reserving whey. Return curds and massage until rubbery.
Strain again, place in cheese mold. Press to accelerate draining.
Place on wire rack overnight with vinegar-soaked tea towel covering.
Prepare brine: boil 3 tbsp salt in 1 liter water, cool completely.
Place cheese in cold brine. Keep refrigerated in brine for months.

notes: Ready to eat 2-3 days after brining begins
Cut into cubes and store in olive oil with herbs for variation

recipes.title: Marinated Feta
recipes.description: Feta preserved in herb-infused olive oil blend.

ingredients.item: prepared feta cheese (brined 1 week, air-dried 1 day)

instructions.text: Wash a large jar, then sterilize it and the lid.
Place fresh herb sprigs and crumbled chilies into jar with black pepper.
Fill jar with equal parts olive oil and sunflower oil.
Add the prepared feta into the oil mixture.
Refrigerate for minimum one week to allow flavors to develop.

notes: Oil blend prevents solidification when refrigerated
Two weeks infusion produces excellent results

recipes.title: Pepper Jack Cheese
recipes.description: Spicy variation of Monterey Jack with hot chili flakes.

instructions.text: Boil chilli flakes in 1/2 cup water for 15 minutes. Strain, reserve chili water and flakes.
Add chili water to milk. Heat using double boiler to 31°C (88°F).
Add calcium chloride if using homogenized milk.
Add mesophilic starter, mix 1 minute. Raise to 32°C (90°F), ripen 30 minutes.
Add diluted rennet, stir 1 minute. Cover, wait 45 minutes for clean break.
Cut curds into 6mm cubes. Maintain 32°C while stirring for 40 minutes.
Gradually raise temp to 38°C (100°F) over 35 minutes. Stir for 30 more minutes.
Rest curds 5 minutes. Pour off whey to curd level.
Rest curds 30 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes at 38°C.
Spoon curds into cheesecloth-lined colander. Toss with salt and boiled chili flakes.
Line 900g mould. Press at 5kg for 15 minutes.
Press at 15kg for 30 minutes. Press at 20kg for 12 hours.
Air dry at room temperature until dry to touch (2-5 days).
Wax and age at 13°C (55°F) at 80-85% humidity for 1-3 months.

notes: Turn weekly during aging to distribute fats and flavor
After ripening, cut wheel into quarters and rewax three-quarters

recipes.title: Homemade Ricotta Cheese
recipes.description: Simple homemade ricotta using vinegar acidification. A foundational cheese that can be used in countless recipes from desserts to savory dishes.

instructions.text: Heat milk in heavy pot to 185°F, stirring regularly to prevent scorching.
Remove from heat and stir in vinegar for about 2 minutes until curds separate from clear yellowish whey.
If separation is incomplete, heat to 200-205°F and add 1-2 teaspoons more vinegar.
Ladle curds into cheesecloth-lined strainer and drain for 1 minute.
Add butter and baking soda to warm curds and stir until incorporated.
Use immediately while warm, or refrigerate for up to one week.

notes: Can be frozen for later use
Butter and baking soda create a creamier, less grainy texture
Can use cow, goat, or sheep milk

recipes.title: Homemade Cheddar Cheese
recipes.source_note: Practical Self Reliance - practicalselfreliance.com (adapted from Home Cheesemaking by Rikki Carroll)
recipes.description: Traditional cheddar with the signature 'cheddaring' step where curds are stacked and flipped to develop texture. Ages to sharp, complex flavor.

ingredients.item: whole milk (raw or pasteurized, not ultra-pasteurized)
calcium chloride liquid (optional, for pasteurized milk)

instructions.text: Warm milk to 86°F. Add starter culture, let sit 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add rennet diluted in water, allow 45 minutes for curds to set with a clean break.
Cut curds into 1/4-inch cubes, rest 5 minutes.
Gradually heat to 100°F over 40 minutes, stirring occasionally.
After curds settle, drain through cheesecloth.
CHEDDARING: Stack curds and maintain at 100°F for 2 hours, flipping every 15 minutes until texture resembles cooked chicken.
Break curds into 1/2-inch pieces, salt with 2 tbsp cheese salt.
Press in mold: 20 lbs for 30 minutes, 40 lbs for 12 hours, 50 lbs for 24 hours.
Air dry 2-5 days at room temperature, flipping daily.
Age at 50-55°F and 85% humidity for at least 3 months (longer for sharper flavor).

notes: Cheddaring step is critical - curds should develop chicken-like texture
Age minimum 3 months for mild, 6-12 months for sharp
Requires humidity-controlled aging environment

recipes.title: Farmhouse Cheddar (18th Century Recipe)
recipes.description: Historical cheddar made without added cultures, relying on natural bacteria in raw milk. Produces a dry, grateable cheese similar to parmesan.

instructions.text: Warm milk to 85-90°F.
Dilute rennet in 1/4 cup water. Add to milk, stir for about 1 minute using figure-8 motions.
If using pasteurized milk, add 1 cup cultured buttermilk and 1/2 tsp calcium chloride diluted in water.
Let sit undisturbed for approximately 90 minutes until stiff curds form.
Cut curds into 1-inch cubes, cutting completely to pot bottom.
Allow 60-90 minutes additional rest time.
Slowly raise temperature to 100°F, increasing no more than 2°F every 5 minutes.
Hold at 100°F for 5-10 minutes, then drain through cheesecloth-lined colander.
Mix salt throughout, breaking curds into small pieces.
Press in cheese press lined with cheesecloth for 2 hours with gradually increasing pressure, then 12 hours under steady pressure.
Flip cheese, press opposite side for 12 hours.
Store on salted shelf minimum 60 days, flipping daily or every 2 days.

notes: No added cultures - relies on natural bacteria in raw milk
Produces dry texture suitable for grating like parmesan
Traditional method from 18th century farmhouses

recipes.title: Traditional Cultured Mozzarella
recipes.description: Authentic mozzarella using natural starter culture rather than citric acid shortcut. Deeper, more complex flavor with proper stretch.

ingredients.item: starter (clabber, kefir, whey, or 1 packet mesophilic)

instructions.text: Heat milk to approximately 95°F (35°C).
Thoroughly mix in starter culture.
Add rennet and mix completely.
Allow 45 minutes to 1 hour for clean break, keeping pot covered.
Cut curds to walnut size (approximately 1 inch/2.5 cm) using vertical, crosswise, and diagonal cuts.
Gently stir curds for 5-10 minutes.
Ferment curds under whey at ambient temperature until acidity develops (goal pH 5.3). Typically requires 6-8 hours total. Maintain temperature above 86°F (30°C).
Prepare 5 quarts boiling water, 5 quarts cold water, and light salt brine (2 quarts cold water + 1 tbsp salt).
Strain curds from whey.
Slowly add hot water to curds, stirring gently until evenly melted.
Form curds into single mass; stretch handfuls into 6-inch ropes.
Fold ropes accordion-style and shape into balls.
Plunge finished mozzarella into cold water until cooled.
Transfer to salt brine and refrigerate.

notes: Natural culture develops deeper flavor than citric acid shortcut
Stretch test: curds should spin fibers when pH reaches 5.3
Whey can be used to make ricotta
Pasta filata (spun-curd) cheese technique

recipes.title: Feta Cheese
recipes.description: Traditional brined feta with authentic tangy flavor. Lipase enzyme is essential for the characteristic sharp taste. Ages in brine for weeks to months.

instructions.text: Warm milk to 86°F (88°F for cow milk) in double boiler.
Add culture and lipase, stir well and let ripen covered for one hour.
Dissolve rennet in 1/2 cup water. Add to milk and stir briskly for 15 seconds.
Cover and let set 30-40 minutes until clean break achieved.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch pieces using vertical cuts, then horizontal (checkerboard), then diagonal at 45° angle, rotating pot between each direction.
Rest 10 minutes, then stir gently for 45 minutes at 86°F, stirring every 10 minutes.
Line colander with dampened cheesecloth. Pour in curds.
Tie corners and hang 3-4 hours, turn over, then hang 24 hours total.
Cut into 2-3 inch cubes. Sprinkle all sides with kosher salt.
Let sit at room temperature 2-3 days.
Prepare brine: boil 1/2 cup salt per 1/2 gallon water, cool completely.
Transfer cheese to sterilized container, add brine, age 1-4 weeks minimum (1 month recommended).
Keep refrigerated. Lasts up to a year in brine.

recipes.temperature: 86°F for goat milk, 88°F for cow milk
notes: Lipase is essential for authentic feta flavor
Don't add brine too soon or cheese may soften
Turn cheese during draining to create proper form
Mold on surface can be skimmed - still safe to eat
Traditional Greek feta uses sheep or goat milk

recipes.title: Italian Havarti Cheese
recipes.description: A mild, creamy Danish-style cheese with Italian herb seasoning. Uses washed-curd technique and ages in just 4-6 weeks.

ingredients.item: fresh raw milk (no older than 2 days)

instructions.text: Warm milk to 90°F, then turn off heat. Sprinkle culture over surface and let rehydrate 5 minutes.
Using an up and down motion, combine the culture into the milk.
Dilute rennet in 1/4 cup cool water and combine using same motion. Cover and wait 30-60 minutes until achieving a clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2 inch cubes with 5-minute resting periods between cuts.
Gently stir 5-10 minutes to achieve uniform sizing. Continue stirring 5 additional minutes until curds resemble half a grape and feel like poached egg whites.
Let curds settle. Remove whey, replacing with 1 gallon 105°F sterilized non-chlorinated water. Stir 10 minutes until curds have firmness of a raisin.
Drain whey completely. Add salt and Italian seasoning to pot. Leave covered 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes.
Add 1 gallon 105°F sterilized water, stir 1 minute, then let curds sit under whey 5 minutes.
Line cheese form with damp cloth and place in shallow baking dish. Pack curds into form.
Press at low pressure 30 minutes, then redress and press at medium pressure 5 additional hours.
Place on rack in plastic container. Flip daily, draining accumulated whey, for 2-5 days until surface feels dry.
Vacuum seal and age in temperature-controlled environment.

notes: Fresh raw milk no older than 2 days is recommended
Good after 4 weeks aging, 6 weeks recommended for raw milk cheese
Washed-curd technique creates characteristic creamy texture

recipes.title: Homemade Sour Cream
recipes.description: One of the easiest dairy products to make. Just culture heavy cream overnight for thick, tangy sour cream.

ingredients.item: mesophilic culture (or 1 tbsp clabber or previous batch sour cream)

instructions.text: Sprinkle freeze dried culture over the surface of the cream. Let rehydrate for 5 minutes before incorporating. (If using clabber or previous batch, no waiting needed.)
Put a lid on the jar and leave it on the counter for 12-24 hours until thick like Greek yogurt, but no bubbles have formed.
Once it reaches desired thickness, refrigerate or strain further into cream cheese.

notes: Can use previous batch as starter for next batch
Fermentation time depends on room temperature
Can be strained further to make cream cheese

recipes.title: Swiss Cheese
recipes.description: Traditional Swiss with characteristic eyes (holes) created by Propionibacterium. An advanced cheese requiring precise temperature control through multiple aging stages.

ingredients.item: fresh yogurt (L. bulgaricus and S. thermophiles)

instructions.text: Warm milk to 95°F. Add cultures, set 20 minutes.
Dissolve rennet in cool water, stir into milk, wait ~30 minutes for clean break.
Make 1/8-inch vertical cuts, whisk to wheat-grain size curds.
Hold at 95°F for 30-40 minutes, then slowly raise to 125°F.
Maintain 125°F for 45 additional minutes.
Let curds settle, drain into cloth-lined hoop. Press 5 minutes.
Replace cloth, press 3 hours. Rinse cloth in saturated salt water and continue pressing for 9 more hours total (3-hour intervals).
BRINING: Float cheese in 45°F saturated salt brine for 2 days, turning daily.
FIRST AGING: 10 days at 50-55°F (90% humidity), wiping daily with salt-soaked cloth.
WARM ROOM: Move to 70°F (70-80% humidity) for 1.5 months. Wipe with clean salt water 2x per week. Cheese should puff up as holes form.
FINAL CURING: Age at 40-45°F for 4 months to 1 year.

recipes.temperature: 95°F initial, 125°F cooking, 50-55°F first aging, 70°F for eyes, 40-45°F final
notes: Propionibacterium creates the characteristic holes and flavor
Not a beginner cheese - requires precise temperature control
Eyes form during warm room stage
Author notes recipe is still being refined
